description: SuperMAG is a worldwide collaboration of organisations and national agencies that brings together data from nearly 600 ground-based magnetometers operated over the last six decades, including INTERMAGNET observatories and stations giving relative measurements. It contains ground magnetic field perturbations processed into one coordinate system, with identical time resolution and a common baseline removal, so that variations caused by ionospheric and magnetospheric currents are separated from the Earth's main field; derived products include SuperMAG auroral and ring current indices, polar plots, movies and substorm lists. Coverage is global, at 1-minute resolution for all stations and 1-second for the subset that provides it. The service is run at JHU/APL to give scientists, teachers, students and the public easy access. Data are accessible through the website and a web service after free email registration. Under the rules of the road data are provided for fair use and cannot be redistributed, and users must acknowledge collaborators and cite Gjerloev (2012), at no cost. Caveats: station coverage is uneven, oceans are poorly covered, and baseline removal choices affect derived values. It serves geomagnetically induced current (GIC) hazard modelling for power grids, pipelines and railways, and space weather event reconstruction; related records are INTERMAGNET, the GFZ Kp index, OMNI and the ESA Space Weather Service Network.
